newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Landesbank Sachsen AAA, affirms L-Bank.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Landesbank Sachsen AAA, affirms L-Bank.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it affirmed its AAA long-term rating of Landeskredietbank Baden-Wuerttemberg and issued a first-time rating of AAA for Landesbank Sachsen.

The ratings were part of a report IBCA has completed on the possibility that the German public-law banks' support and guarantee mechanisms might have evolved to the point where they infringe the anti-constraint of competition articles of the European Union treaties.
The following is the report issued by IBCA:

"IBCA has issued a sequel to its December, 1996, research comment, "Karel van Miert vs. Helmut Kohl - what are the odds?". This examined the possibility that the German public-law banks' support and guarantee mechanisms might have evolved to the point where they infringe the anti-constraint of competition articles of the European Union treaties.

"The comment identified two distinct types of public-law banks: those whose support mechanisms are at present legal under the Treaty of Rome and those (only three) with cover that is already potentially illegal.
"In its latest comment IBCA reviews reactions to the original publication and subsequent events under two headings, "The legal argument" and "The political argument".

"It dismisses the legal points made by the public-law banks against the thesis that their support and guarantee mechanisms infringe the European treaties and states that the weakness of their arguments has convinced it of the correctness of the conclusions it had already reached.

"In the section on the political argument, the agency notes two developments. First, there has been much increased activity on the part of the public-law banks and of German politicians, denying that there is any question of the support and guarantee mechanisms infringing the European Union treaties.

"However, in the same breath they have made impassioned pleas to the Federal Government to include in "Maastricht II" a protocol forbidding any attack on these same mechanisms. Second, all has gone quiet on the subject at the European Commission. IBCA concludes: "We deduce that considerable pressure has been exerted and that the Commission is for the time being at least back-pedalling in its pursuit of the Anstaltslast and Gewehrtragerhaftung system.

"Thus, although we are convinced the system will eventually be ruled to be an infringement of Article 92 (of the Treaty of Rome), we think it is highly unlikely that this will happen at least until after the first stage of European Monetary Union has gone through."

"In the concluding "Rating arguments" section IBCA states: "As we said in our original comment, we are happy to affirm our ratings of what we have dubbed the "legal" Landesbanks on the ground that, whatever happens, their creditors will be "grandfathered".

"In regard to the so-called "illegal" banks it states: "In the circumstances as they now are, we consider it so unlikely that the Commission will either choose to make or will be pushed into making an isolated attack on the illegal' banks, that we are taking the following rating action:
"We are affirming our AAA long-term rating of L-Bank;
"We have, today, issued a first-time rating of AAA for Landesbank Sachsen.

"In other words, for the purpose of our ratings the realities of practical politics have overwhelmed the doubts prompted by theoretical possibilities. However, we have shone a light on those possibilities which henceforth neither the banks nor the market can ignore."
